changes: Root npm test now runs the complete 47-member canonical inventory through a resource-aware parallel scheduler with strict terminal failure semantics, process-tree cleanup on every exit path, bounded reports, isolated temporary roots, and optimized acceptance/incremental long tails.
usage: From a standard clean checkout run npm run build, then run npm test; the default jobs=4 canonical suite reports each member and writes an optional atomic JSON artifact when --json-output is supplied.
expectedOutcome: The complete canonical suite executes safely in parallel and finishes below 300000ms on three consecutive same-material clean-checkout runs, without retries masking failures or descendant processes leaking.
actualTranscript: Final same-material jobs=4 runs passed 47/47 in 216146ms, 220808ms, and 223474ms with launches=47, retries=0, identityDrift=false; serial oracle passed 47/47; F-053 heartbeat repro proved normal-exit descendants are reaped; DONE-required and 93-command validation passed.
outcomeDiff: No difference: the delivered behavior matches the expected complete, safe, sub-five-minute canonical test execution.
pitfalls: The main pitfalls were stale material bindings after lifecycle metadata and a normal-exit grandchild leak; strict replay exposed both, final receipts were regenerated, and future changes to runner output or canonical members must refresh serial and three-run evidence.
